startup.name: Uplane
startup.description: AI system that generates many ads and matching landing pages and steers spend across Meta, Google and LinkedIn, learning from CRM and ERP data. Sells to enterprises for higher return on ad spend and to SMBs as expert level marketing without an agency. Team of 26 in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts at the as_of date, so the acceptance step is reported only for completeness: the prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent), and conditional on being accepted the forecast below is what matters. Team of 26 is unusually large for a batch company, which signals existing funding or revenue and raises odds modestly, but the ads category is crowded.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would likely hesitate because AI ad generation and agency replacement are widely pitched, platforms such as Meta and Google build competing tools, and a 26 person team raises the question of why it needs the YC deal; the pitch also claims both enterprise and SMB.

ladder.why_it_fails: The most plausible miss is that Uplane takes the YC deal, shows enterprise ad spend pilots but no repeatable revenue inside 13 months, and investors wait. AI ad generation is crowded with funded rivals (Creatify raised a $15.5M Series A in May 2025, GIGR $5.4M pre-seed), analogs like Plai and Replo reached only a seed with small rounds, and Criya (roomplays) was inactive after a seed. A round above $1M needs proof that agencies are actually replaced, which is slow to show in enterprise sales cycles.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry B2B --years 2022-2024 --calibration-only: series_a cond 33 percent (n=54), upper 35 percent; months_to_series_a p25 22, median 30, p75 39 (n=18). Ever 0.33 times about 0.2 reaching an A inside 13 months of batch start is 0.07.
anchors.adjustment_reason: More than 2x below the ever rate because the window is only 13.4 months and median time to Series A is 28 to 30 months from batch start; I give 0.08 since a 26 person team with revenue could be one of the fast ones.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A of $6M to $10M at a modest valuation, below the 2022+ median. Series A bands use the 2022+ YC table (p25 $11M, median $15M, p75 $21M) and public medians of about $17M.
Typical Series A of $10M to $20M, near the 2022+ YC median of about $14M. Series A bands use the 2022+ YC table (p25 $11M, median $15M, p75 $21M) and public medians of about $17M.
Strong Series A of $20M to $40M for a fast growing product with revenue. Series A bands use the 2022+ YC table (p25 $11M, median $15M, p75 $21M) and public medians of about $17M.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series A inside the window would need roughly $1M or more of ARR and proof of improved return on ad spend for enterprises within a year of the batch. Medians put an A near 30 months after batch start, enterprise marketing pilots take two quarters to close, and Meta and Google ship their own creative and budget tools. Plai and Replo, close analogs, stopped at seed, so a fast A is the exception.

anchors.adjustment_reason: These later steps are conditional on a seed and A already inside the window, which implies unusual speed, so the conditional is kept near the anchor (0.15); the window gives them little mass, and reaching a round years later is common for companies with paying customers.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series B needs a durable growth engine in a category where platforms and agencies can copy features; the cohort shows only about one in six B2B seed companies reaches B, and nothing in the window makes this near. The failure case is a revenue plateau at SMB level with churn when ad platforms bundle their own automation, so investors see a feature rather than a company.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C requires a category winning position and efficient growth; the 2022 to 2024 B2B cohort has no Series C yet. Ad automation spend is cyclical and large platforms hold the distribution, so a few companies reach this stage, and almost none inside 13 months.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely outcome is a stall or an acqui-hire: AI ad tools are crowded, platform owners keep adding automation, and the cohort of AI marketing companies (Plai, Replo, Criya) shows seed stage endpoints and quiet exits. A $100M or larger outcome needs enterprise revenue that survives the platform bundling.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating ads and landing pages is easy with current models; the hard part is closing the loop from CRM and ERP profit data to budget allocation across channels with reliable attribution. A 26 person team can build the generator in three months but the data integrations and trust in autonomous spend control take much longer.

takeover_risk.rationale: Ad platforms already ship automated creative and budget tools and have the incentive to keep spend in their own systems; funded startups copy features within months. Cross channel and profit data loops are the part a platform cannot easily copy.

evidence.claim: Investors funded multiple AI ad automation startups in 2025, showing active paid demand for replacing agency work
A cited firm reports over 1 million marketers using an AI ad tool, though figures are unverified

roadmap.proof: $1M plus ARR, net revenue retention above 110 percent

brand.rationale: A short invented name in the common 5 to 6 letter bucket; the cohort data show no survival difference for such names, comparable to other plain coined YC names, so brand will not move the odds.

narrative.headline: A large team in a crowded AI ad market; the seed odds sit near the B2B anchor for the 13 month window and do not rank it against peers.
narrative.general_summary: Uplane pitches AI that replaces marketing agencies, generating ads and landing pages and steering spend across channels from CRM and ERP data. The team is 26 people, which is large for a batch company, but AI ad automation is crowded with funded rivals and platform tools. Inside 13.4 months the seed probability is about 0.47, close to the B2B cohort anchor of 0.61 times the share of seeds that arrive that early, and Series A inside the window is unlikely at about 0.08. Past analogs in the same wedge reached only seed or died.

assumptions: Blind forecast made as of 2025-10-06 using only the YC batch description in the input file, with market-only web searches.
Forecast window is 13.4 months, from 2025-10-06 to 2026-11-17.

Seed means an outside financing round above about $1M that closes inside the window, not the standard YC deal of about $500K; the seed and Series A probabilities are window probabilities, not ever probabilities.

The odds do not rank this company against other companies in the batch: in the 2026 winners test, team size, claimed traction and a hot sector did not separate raisers from non raisers, so the seed number stays near the cohort anchor.
Cohort anchors come from older and 2022 to 2024 batches and are partly right censored; funding coverage in the data is incomplete (lower, known and upper ranges quoted).
